newsitem.title: USA: Pepsi to restructure, take charge; earnings down.
newsitem.headline: Pepsi to restructure, take charge; earnings down.

text.p: PepsiCo Inc., said Thursday it planned to restructure its international operations and take special charges that will cause its third quarter earnings to fall short of year-earlier results.

The company will refocus on its core businesses of Pepsi-Cola beverage products, Taco Bell, Pizza Hut and Kentucky Fried Chicken restaurants and Frito-Lay snacks, said Roger Enrico, PepsiCo's chief executive officer.
"Now is the time to re-evaluate all other businesses in our portfolio, as well as to streamline our operations, especially international beverages," Enrico said.

Pepsi said its international operations will be restructured to trim operating expenses by $100 million a year and shift its focus to "those markets in which we are already strong." The company also will write down the value of investments in operations in Argentina and Brazil.
Those aspects of the restructuring will result in a special charges totalling about $525 million, or 31 cents a share, in the third and fourth quarters.
"Clearly we've had problems in our international beverage business," Enrico said. "But I believe we're moving to fix them quickly and get ourselves on a sound strategic footing.
